html: The Opiscopank were a small Algonquian group on the south side of the lower Rappahannock River in Virginia, in today's Middlesex County. John Smith recorded them in 1608 as part of the wider chiefdom of Powhatan. Like their neighbours the Rappahannock, they lived by growing maize, fishing and hunting. English settlement of the river after the 1640s pushed them off their land, and they disappear from the records.
